name: Question 5
worked_solution:
The $4$th row of the matrix contains two zeros, more than any other row. So using a Laplace expansion along the $4$th row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{41}+(-2)\cdot {C}_{42}+1\cdot {C}_{43}+0\cdot {C}_{44} \\  & =(-2)\cdot (-1)^{4+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}|+1\cdot (-1)^{4+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}|-|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$
